title: 4GE1-style exam questions: river environments (Paper 1, Topic 1)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 23 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 23: Revision: river environments (Paper 1, Topic 1). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Timed answer (10 minutes): 'Assess the success of river management in one named country you have studied.' Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Named scheme and place; aims; successes and problems with evidence (for example, a flood relief channel or a large dam such as Three Gorges, China); substantiated judgement
questions.model: Teacher plans it first: name the scheme; P1 aims and what was built; P2 successes with evidence; P3 problems with evidence; conclusion: overall judgement using 'mostly' or 'partly'.

questions.q: Peer-mark with the indicative mark points. Write one 'even better if' target.
questions.a: A specific target such as 'add a statistic' or 'make a clearer judgement'

questions.q: Explain how one physical and one human factor together increase flood risk.
questions.a: For example: saturated ground plus urbanisation: no infiltration and fast runoff combine to raise peak discharge

questions.q: Calculate the lag time: peak rain 14:00, peak discharge 02:00 next day.
questions.model: 14:00 to midnight = 10 hours. Midnight to 02:00 = 2 hours. 10 + 2 = 12 hours.

questions.q: Explain one human cause of flooding.
questions.a: Urbanisation (1): impermeable surfaces increase runoff so water reaches the river faster (1)

questions.q: Describe one feature of a flood plain.
questions.a: Flat, wide land beside the river (1), made of deposited alluvium from floods (1)
Use evidence to judge the importance of factors
options: Use evidence to judge the importance of factors

questions.q: Big question: can you explain a river from source to mouth in five minutes?
questions.a: A sequence covering changes in gradient, discharge, processes and landforms from upper to lower course
